title: Recession warning
text: Credit is tightening and order books are thinning. Forecasters who were cheerful a quarter ago are now using the word "contraction".

opts.label: Cut early
opts.hint: Freeze hiring and trim spending now to protect cash.

out.text: You moved before the numbers forced you to. The team is rattled.

opts.label: Hold course
opts.hint: Change nothing and watch the data.

out.text: You keep the plan. The downturn arrives on schedule.

opts.label: Lean in
opts.hint: Spend on marketing while rivals retrench. Wins share if you can afford the trough.

out.text: You advertise into the silence. Customers notice who is still standing.

lesson: Recessions reward cash and punish leverage. Spending against the cycle wins share cheaply, but only companies that survive the trough get to enjoy it.

title: Surprise rate rise
text: The central bank has raised rates by three-quarters of a point, more than anyone expected, and says it is not finished.

opts.label: Fix your floating debt
opts.hint: Lock today’s rate for a fee. Costs more now; protects you if rates keep climbing.

out.text: The bank swaps your floating loans to fixed.

opts.label: Pay debt down
opts.hint: Use cash to retire a quarter of your debt. Less interest, less cushion.

out.text: You send the bank a large transfer.

opts.label: Do nothing
opts.hint: Rates might come back down.

out.text: You wait. Interest on anything floating just went up.

lesson: Floating-rate debt is cheap until it is not. Fixing costs a premium because you are buying insurance against exactly this.

title: Emergency rate cut
text: With the economy sliding, the central bank has cut rates sharply.

opts.label: Refinance at fixed
opts.hint: Lock in the low rate on existing loans.

out.text: Your loans are now fixed near the bottom of the cycle.

opts.label: Stay floating
opts.hint: Enjoy falling payments while they last.

out.text: Your interest bill shrinks.

lesson: Central banks cut when things are bad. Cheap money is an opportunity precisely when most people are too frightened to borrow.

title: Inflation surges
text: Prices are rising at the fastest pace in years. Your suppliers have all sent "updated terms", and your staff have noticed their rent.

opts.label: Raise prices now
opts.hint: Put prices up 6% ahead of the market. Protects margin, tests loyalty.

out.text: The new price list goes out. Some customers grumble; most pay.

opts.label: Give a cost-of-living raise
opts.hint: Staff keep up with prices; your wage bill jumps.

out.text: The all-hands applauds. Finance does not.

opts.label: Absorb it
opts.hint: Hold prices and pay to protect share.

out.text: You hold the line and watch the margin thin.

lesson: Inflation is a test of pricing power. Companies that can raise prices without losing customers are worth far more than those that cannot.

title: Credit crunch
text: A mid-sized bank has failed and every other lender is suddenly counting its capital. Credit committees are saying no to everything.

opts.label: Draw the whole credit line
opts.hint: Take the cash while the facility exists. You pay interest on money you may not need.

out.text: The money lands before anyone can change their mind.

opts.label: Buy covenant headroom
opts.hint: Pay a fee now to secure three quarters of optionality.

out.text: The bank agrees, for a price.

opts.label: Trust your bank
opts.hint: You have a relationship. Surely that counts.

out.text: Your banker keeps the line open.
Your banker is very sorry. The line is cut in half.

lesson: Credit lines are there until you need them. In a crunch, liquidity you have already drawn is the only liquidity you can count on.

title: Markets in freefall
text: Share prices have fallen by a quarter in three weeks. Nobody can say exactly why, which is making it worse.

opts.label: Raise cash at any price
opts.hint: Sell 12% of the company at a 30% discount. Painful, safe.

out.text: A fund takes the shares, and its pound of flesh.

opts.label: Hire the talent others are cutting
opts.hint: Good people are suddenly available.

out.text: You pick up people who would never have taken your call a year ago.

opts.label: Wait it out
opts.hint: Prices are opinions. Your business has not changed.

out.text: You carry on.

lesson: A crash changes the price of your company, not the value of it — unless you need to raise money, in which case the price is all that matters.

title: Euphoria
text: Markets are at record highs and investors are funding anything with a pitch deck. Your phone has not stopped.

opts.label: Raise while it is cheap
opts.hint: Sell 10% at a 25% premium to your valuation.

out.text: The round closes in a fortnight.

opts.label: Talk up your ambitions
opts.hint: A bold public forecast lifts your valuation. Then you have to hit it.

out.text: The market loves it, and you deliver.
The market loves it. Two quarters later you miss, badly.

opts.label: Ignore the noise
opts.hint: Keep your head down.

out.text: You get back to work.

lesson: The best time to raise money is when you do not need it. The worst promises are the ones made at the top.

title: The forecast you made
text: Analysts have noticed the gap between what you promised at the peak and what you delivered.

opts.label: Own it
opts.hint: Reset expectations honestly.

out.text: A rough week, then it passes.

opts.label: Blame the economy
opts.hint: Everyone else does.

out.text: Nobody is fooled.

opts.text: Analysts will be more scrutinizing next time.

lesson: Guidance is a promise. Markets forgive a bad quarter faster than a broken one.

lesson.title: Currency crisis
lesson.text: The currency in {region} has lost a fifth of its value in a month. Everything you earn there is worth less at home.

opts.label: Hedge what is left
opts.hint: Pay a premium to lock today’s rate for two years.

out.text: You buy forwards. Expensive, but the bleeding stops.

opts.label: Raise local prices
opts.hint: Recover some of it from customers, 8% across the board.

out.text: Local customers pay more. Some leave.

opts.label: Ride it out
opts.hint: Currencies come back. Usually.

out.text: You do nothing and translate the damage.

lesson.lesson: Foreign revenue carries currency risk. Local costs are a natural hedge; what is exposed is your margin, not your sales.

lesson.title: Government stimulus
lesson.text: A large spending package has passed. Public contracts are about to be tendered in every sector, including yours.

opts.label: Chase public contracts
opts.hint: Spend on bids. Good odds of a long stretch of extra demand.

out.text: You win a framework contract.
The incumbents win everything.

opts.label: Hire ahead of the boom
opts.hint: Open positions now, before wages rise.

out.text: Requisitions go out while candidates are still cheap.

opts.label: Carry on
opts.hint: The tide lifts you anyway.

out.text: Demand picks up on its own.

lesson.lesson: Fiscal stimulus raises demand now and inflation later. Position for the first, and plan for the second.

lesson.title: Nobody to hire
lesson.text: Unemployment is at a record low. Recruiters are calling your people at their desks.

opts.label: Raise pay everywhere
opts.hint: Eight points against market, company-wide.

out.text: Offer letters start being accepted again.

opts.label: Retention bonuses
opts.hint: A one-off payment to stay put this year.

out.text: Most people sign.

opts.label: Hold the line
opts.hint: The market will cool.

out.text: You lose people you would rather have kept.

lesson.lesson: In a tight labour market, the cheapest employee is the one you already have. Replacement costs months of salary before the new hire is productive.

lesson.title: A new technology wave
lesson.text: A new class of tools has gone from demo to mainstream in eighteen months. Customers are asking what your plan is.

opts.label: Bet big
opts.hint: Retool the product around it. Expensive, and the technology may not be ready.

out.text: It works. You are suddenly the modern choice.
It half-works. You have spent a lot to learn a little.

opts.label: Fast-follow
opts.hint: Let others find the dead ends, then copy what works.

out.text: A sensible, unexciting improvement.

opts.label: Wait and see
opts.hint: Most waves are hype.

out.text: It was mostly hype.
It was not hype. Rivals pulled ahead.

lesson.lesson: Technology shifts are when market leadership changes hands. How much risk are you willing to take to be early?

lesson.title: Pandemic
lesson.text: A fast-spreading illness has closed borders and emptied offices. Governments are improvising.

opts.label: Protect everyone
opts.hint: Send people home, keep paying them, accept the disruption.

out.text: Output dips. People remember how you behaved.

opts.label: Cut pay temporarily
opts.hint: A quarter of everyone’s pay for two quarters.

out.text: The cash holds. The goodwill does not.

opts.label: Business as usual
opts.hint: It will blow over.

out.text: You get away with it.
An outbreak in the office. It is in the papers.

lesson.lesson: Rare shocks cannot be forecast, only survived. Cash reserves, flexible costs and a workforce that trusts you are what resilience is made of.

lesson.title: Energy price shock
lesson.text: A supply disruption has sent energy prices up by a third. Everything that moves, heats or computes costs more.

opts.label: Efficiency drive
opts.hint: Spend now to use less for good.

out.text: The savings outlast the crisis.

opts.label: Add a surcharge
opts.hint: Pass 3% on to customers.

out.text: The surcharge goes on every invoice.

opts.label: Absorb it
opts.hint: Hope it is temporary.

out.text: Margins take the hit.

lesson.lesson: Input shocks are margin shocks unless you can pass them on. Who pays — you, your customer or your supplier — is decided by bargaining power.

lesson.title: Trade war
lesson.text: Tariffs have gone up on both sides of a major trade route, and the retaliation has only started.

opts.label: Localise supply
opts.hint: Rebuild sourcing inside each region. Costly now, immune later.

out.text: Slower, dearer, safer.

opts.label: Lobby for an exemption
opts.hint: Your industry association is asking for money.

out.text: Your products are carved out.
No exemption. The tariffs bite.

opts.label: Wait
opts.hint: Trade wars end in deals.

out.text: This one drags on.

lesson.lesson: Global supply chains are efficient and fragile. Political risk does not appear in a supplier’s quote.

lesson.title: Green shoots
lesson.text: For the first time in a year the surveys have turned up. Customers are returning calls.

opts.label: Hire before everyone else
opts.hint: Open positions while talent is still cheap and available.

out.text: You get your pick.

opts.label: Go shopping
opts.hint: Weak competitors are for sale.

out.text: A struggling founder would like to talk.

opts.label: Stay cautious
opts.hint: False dawns happen.

out.text: You wait for confirmation.

lesson.lesson: The recovery is when share is won. Capacity and people take quarters to add; those who start early are ready when demand returns.

lesson.title: Diesel at a record high
lesson.text: Fuel has gone up a quarter in a month. Most of your contracts were priced before it did.

opts.label: Impose a fuel surcharge
opts.hint: Pass it on; some customers will resent it.

out.text: Most customers accept the surcharge.

opts.label: Absorb it
opts.hint: Protect relationships, lose money for a while.

out.text: Margins vanish until prices fall.

opts.label: Fuel-efficiency drive
opts.hint: Route optimisation and training.

out.text: Consumption drops a little, for good.

lesson.lesson: In a thin-margin business an input shock is a solvency question. Contracts that let you pass costs through are worth more than they look.

lesson.title: Port strike
lesson.text: Dock workers at the main port serving {region} have walked out. Containers are piling up.

opts.label: Reroute through other ports
opts.hint: Longer, dearer, moving.

out.text: Freight keeps moving at a higher cost.

opts.label: Wait it out
opts.hint: Strikes end.

out.text: Your trucks sit idle for six weeks.

lesson.lesson: Networks are only as strong as their chokepoints. Alternatives cost money until the day they are the only way through.

lesson.title: Carbon price jumps
lesson.text: The carbon price has doubled after a new climate agreement. Fossil generators’ costs just jumped.

opts.label: Sell the news
opts.hint: Clean power is now the cheap option. Tell customers.

out.text: Demand for clean contracts rises.

opts.label: Raise prices
opts.hint: The market price of power rose; so does yours.

out.text: Margins expand.

lesson.lesson: Carbon pricing moves the cost curve. Low-cost producers benefit twice: their costs did not rise, and their competitors’ did.

lesson.title: Your bank has failed
lesson.text: Regulators have closed the bank that holds most of your cash. Deposits above the insured limit are frozen while the administrators work out what is left.

opts.label: Wait for the administrators
opts.hint: Failed banks usually pay back most of their deposits — eventually.

out.text: Two quarters later, 95 cents on the dollar comes back.
The hole is deeper than anyone said: 80 cents on the dollar.

opts.label: Sell the claim to a distressed-debt fund
opts.hint: Cash today, at a discount.

out.text: The fund pays 88 cents on the dollar, today.

lesson.lesson: Cash in a bank is a loan to that bank. Above the insured limit it is only as safe as the bank, which is why treasurers spread deposits across several banks and hold some in short-term government bills.

lesson.title: A tariff war
lesson.text: Governments are trading tariffs. The goods and parts you bring into {region} now carry a 20% duty.

opts.label: Absorb it
opts.hint: Hold prices and eat the cost while the dispute lasts.

out.text: Margins thin while the politicians argue.

opts.label: Pass it on to customers
opts.hint: Raise prices to cover the duty.

out.text: Customers grumble; some trade down.

opts.label: Move production home
opts.hint: Build local supply: expensive now, cheaper if the dispute drags on.

out.text: The new supply line is running within the year.

lesson.lesson: Where you make things is a strategic choice. Cheap global supply chains carry political risk; local ones cost more but cannot be taxed at the border.
